newsitem.title: CANADA: TimberWest explores sale, equity options.
newsitem.headline: TimberWest explores sale, equity options.

text.p: TimberWest Forest Ltd, which has put itself up for sale, is negotiating with bidders and also examining other "equity alternatives," a director said Tuesday.

Stephen Bellringer, an independent director overseeing the sale process, said he did not know when the lumber producer would announce a deal. TimberWest said late last month it hoped to make an announcement in mid-January.

Bellringer said the company is still "very actively" looking at a deal to sell the entire company but is also examining other equity options so it could compare the returns possible from the two approaches.
"We are discussing various alternatives with a number of parties," Bellringer said. He did not give details on the other options being explored.
Bellringer said previously that interest has been shown not only in the whole company, but also in specific assets.
Analysts had said forest products company Canfor Corp was in the lead to buy TimberWest for a price of at least C$21 a share or C$643 million.

TimberWest has five lumber mills with annual capacity of 685 million board feet and its prize asset is 210,000 hectares of private timberland. That forest along with government timber tenures provide an annual harvest of 4.2 million cubic meters of wood.
TimberWest put itself up for sale in October.
The decision stemmed in part from 52-percent owner Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd's desire to focus more on its paper business.
Fletcher Canada is majority owned by Fletcher Challenge Ltd of New Zealand.
